author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Jakob Ingebrigtsen returned from Achilles surgery with a season-best 12:59.24 victory in the 5,000 meters Friday, highlighting the opening night of the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest. The Norwegian finished ahead of Americans Cole Hocker and Parker Wolfe and earned the event’s $150,000 first prize.

Pole-vault world-record holder Mondo Duplantis cleared 6.20 meters to win his event, with Greece’s Emmanouil Karalis second at 6.15. Duplantis then made three attempts at 6.32 meters, which would have raised his world record, but gusting wind complicated the record effort. Ukraine’s Yaroslava Mahuchikh also won the women’s high jump on a night built around head-to-head appearances by leading athletes.

A sold-out crowd of 20,557 attended the first session. World Athletics created the championship as a compact season-ending showcase with a $10 million total prize pool, the largest for a track and field meet. Friday’s results supplied the competition outcomes that the new format needed: recognizable champions, close contests and an immediate test of whether larger purses can strengthen the sport’s post-championship calendar.
dek: Track and field stars delivered on the opening night of the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship before a sold-out Budapest crowd.
headline: Ingebrigtsen, Duplantis and Mahuchikh win on Ultimate opener
